description: Permissions for Agent OS's main window. The app UI talks to its own Node server over plain HTTP for everything it shows and changes. It uses Tauri IPC for these things only: the update banner (updater:default, and process:allow-restart to relaunch after an install the person approved; see src/ui/components/UpdateBanner.tsx), the opener (below), the folder picker of the New session dialog (dialog:allow-open: the system's open dialog and nothing else from the dialog plugin; it hands the page only the path the person picked and grants no file access, because the fs plugin is not installed and the asset protocol is off; the message and save dialogs and dialog:default are NOT granted), and the quit question (Tauri's own event permissions, already in core:default: the shell emits agentos://quit-requested and the page answers with agentos://quit-shown and agentos://quit-answer; there is no custom command; see desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs). The opener may do two things only. (1) Show one file in Finder, from the Workspace page (opener:allow-reveal-item-in-dir). (2) Open a link in the person's browser (opener:allow-open-url), but ONLY for the addresses in its `allow` list: the websites and this-Mac pages that Agent OS itself links to from its own fixed data (OpenRouter, the Setup plan's source and terms pages, each agent's homepage and docs, the sign-in pages, the Hermes dashboard on 127.0.0.1:9119, the OpenClaw Control UI on 127.0.0.1:18789, and the one-time OpenRouter sign-in page on this app's own server). Each entry names one exact host and then a slash; there is no wildcard host and no other scheme, and the broad sets that open any address or any path (opener:default, opener:allow-default-urls, opener:allow-open-path) are NOT granted. An address outside the list is refused, and the page then shows it with a Copy button (src/ui/components/OpenAddress.tsx). test/release-config.test.js pins this whole list. The `remote` block is REQUIRED, not decoration: main.rs navigates the window to the local server at http://127.0.0.1:{port}/, so Tauri treats the window's origin as REMOTE, and a capability without a `remote` block only applies to content served from inside the app bundle. Without it every updater call, the folder picker and the quit events are silently rejected by the permission check (Vibespace shipped three releases that way). The port is chosen at runtime, hence the wildcard; 127.0.0.1 is this machine only.
